subject: SR: SDLC evidence package request — code review, CI/CD, secrets, change control
messages:
From: Kara Simmons <kara.simmons@assessly.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com, lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SDLC evidence request — scope & sample ask

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our SIG/SOC2 review we'll need evidence showing how Redwood enforces secure software development practices for production-facing services. For this tranche we're focusing on: code review gating, CI/CD enforcement, secrets handling (short-lived creds, vaulting, rotation), and change/approval trails for releases.

Could you provide the following as a representative sample:
- Manifest describing what artifacts you're providing and why (CSV or spreadsheet)
- 8–12 merged PRs across 3 different services (include PR metadata, reviewer history, and the final merge commit)
- 2 CI build logs that exercised merge gates and automated security checks (sast/lint/unit)
- Audit export showing creation/rotation events for secrets over the past 30 days (redacted where necessary)
- Any documented change approvals (tickets, runbook signoffs) tied to those merges

Also let us know if you have any standard redaction guidance for sensitive items and the expected delivery ETA. Prefer to receive via a secure Drive link.

Best,
Kara
Kara Simmons
Senior Assessor — Assessly
From: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
To: Kara Simmons <kara.simmons@assessly.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com, lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-10-03T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDLC evidence request — scope & sample ask

Kara — thanks for the clear list. We can provide a curated sample that demonstrates our enforcement model and the artifacts you asked for. High-level summary of what we'll deliver (handover plan below):

1) Manifest (attached) — CSV mapping each artifact to the requirement (code-review, CI, secrets, change).
2) PR samples — 10 PRs across web-api, inference-runtime, and console teams. Each PR includes reviewers, timestamps, linked Jira ticket, and the merge commit. Note: we will redact sensitive snippets from diffs but keep metadata intact.
3) CI logs — 3 CI runs (we'll include one with a failing pre-merge lint/SAST that required remediation before merge). CI job names: sdlc-verify, unit-and-scan, deploy-smoke.
4) Secrets audit export — we will provide a CSV export from HashiCorp Vault audit device showing create/read/rotate events for dynamic DB creds and a separate KMS key rotation event log. We'll redact actual secret values.
5) Change approvals — links to the release board item and an exported approval timeline (who approved and when).

Notes on controls:
- Branch protection enforced on protected branches; for core services we require two reviewers, at least one from the owning team and one cross-team reviewer.
- Merges are blocked until sdlc-verify and unit-and-scan pass. Exceptions are only granted by the release manager and are recorded in the release board with justification.
- Secrets: production secrets are stored in Vault with dynamic short-lived DB credentials (TTL-based) plus periodic rotation for long-lived keys stored in our KMS. Access is granted via IAM roles; there's no plaintext secrets in CI logs by design.
- Change mgmt: every release has a linked ticket with acceptance criteria and rollback playbook; we capture deployment approvals via the release board audit trail.

ETA: we'll assemble and upload a redacted bundle and manifest to a secure Drive folder by EOD 2027-10-05. Is that timeline acceptable?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Applied Security
Redwood Inference
From: Kara Simmons <kara.simmons@assessly.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-10-03T12:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDLC evidence request — quick clarifications

Jonas — that plan sounds good, thanks. Quick clarifications before you pack artifacts:

1) For the Vault audit export, can you confirm the retention window for audit logs and whether you produce a signed export (we prefer a tamper-evident export)
2) Do you have any documented exception approvals that would have allowed a direct merge to protected branches in the past 90 days? If so, we'll need the associated ticket and rationale.
3) For the CI logs, please include the job output that shows the gating (e.g., failure then remediation then pass) so we can see enforcement in practice.

If you can include a short readme in the Drive folder mapping artifacts to the control objectives that will speed our review.

Regards,
Kara
From: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
To: Kara Simmons <kara.simmons@assessly.com>, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-10-04T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDLC evidence request — delivery & redaction plan

Kara / Jonas — following up with delivery detail and redaction guidance. We'll provide the following items in the Drive bundle (manifest attached):

- sdlc-sample-manifest.csv (maps each artifact to control IDs and includes a short explanation)
- Ten PR metadata exports (PR metadata, reviewer list, timestamps, linked Jira IDs) named pr-001-metadata.txt through pr-010-metadata.txt
- Two diff extracts (pr-001-diff.txt, pr-004-diff.txt) with code context preserved but secrets and credentials redacted using <REDACTED>. We will preserve line numbers.
- ci-run-20270921.log.txt and ci-run-20270923.log.txt — full job output for sdlc-verify and unit-and-scan jobs (we'll scrub any ephemeral tokens from environment dumps).
- audit-export-20270901-20270930.csv — Vault audit device export showing event type (create/read/rotate/revoke), path, timestamp, and actor. We will not include secret values; the export will include a HMAC signature file (audit-export-202709-signature.sha256) to attest the export integrity.
- release-board-approvals.csv — timeline of approvals and exception tickets (if any).

On exceptions: we had two documented emergency exception approvals in the past 90 days; both are tracked in the release board and we'll include the redacted approval notes and tickets. One was a rollback/patch where the release manager approved a hotfix merge after a documented risk assessment.

Timeline: we'll upload the Drive bundle and share with your assessly account by 2027-10-05 18:00 PDT. If you need anything sooner (e.g., the audit export only), tell us and we'll prioritize.

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Senior Manager, Developer Platform Security
Redwood Inference
From: Kara Simmons <kara.simmons@assessly.com>
To: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-10-05T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDLC evidence request — delivery confirmation

Thanks Irene — that list looks complete and the HMAC signature on the audit export is perfect for our chain-of-custody checks. 2027-10-05 EOD works. We'll review the bundle and let you know if we need additional context or sampling.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Kara
